## The I() construct

`?formula` gives you insights into the way to structure generic formula objects in R.  The `I()` construct is a consistent and clear way in R's foundations to specify functional operations on variables.

## R and GMM

There are a number of packages for estimating GMM models in R.  `pgmm` does many of the most basic models, though Stata is the industry leader in this.  That said, there is a relatively new and highly customizable package for this: `pdynmc` which is [described here in a pdf vignette](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/pdynmc/vignettes/pdynmc-intro.pdf).  What follows is a detailed example with a software guide.



```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(plm)
library(lme4)
library(dplyr)
library(kableExtra)

# pgmm() formulas use lag(x, 1:2) — vector k that dplyr::lag() rejects.
# Setting lag <- plm::lag here makes every pgmm() formula in the document work.
# NOTE: dplyr::lag() must still be used explicitly inside dplyr pipelines
# because plm::lag() applied to a plain vector returns the input unchanged.
lag <- plm::lag

data(EmplUK)
EmplUK <- EmplUK |>
  mutate(n = log(emp), w = log(wage), k = log(capital), ys = log(output))
pdat <- pdata.frame(EmplUK, index = c("firm", "year"))

# Precomputed lag columns for use in plm(model = "random") formulas.
# Using lag() inside a RE formula with lag <- plm::lag causes swar_Between_check()
# to fail. Precomputed columns avoid that entirely.
pdat$n_lag1 <- plm::lag(pdat$n, 1)
pdat$n_lag2 <- plm::lag(pdat$n, 2)
pdat$w_lag1 <- plm::lag(pdat$w, 1)

panel_summary <- function(x, id) {
  grand <- mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  btw   <- tapply(x, id, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  win   <- x - btw[as.character(id)]
  c(Grand_mean  = round(grand, 3),
    SD_total    = round(sd(x,   na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    SD_between  = round(sd(btw, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    SD_within   = round(sd(win, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    Pct_within  = round(100 * var(win, na.rm = TRUE) / var(x, na.rm = TRUE), 1))
}
```

A practical reference for estimating dynamic panel data (DPD) and
generalized method of moments (GMM) models in R and Stata, covering every
estimator discussed in the course. Where one environment handles something the
other cannot, that is noted explicitly.

## Package and command ecosystem

### R packages

```{r packages, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c(
  "plm",             # pgmm(), pmg(), pcdtest() — the core DPD workhorse
  "panelvar",        # Panel VAR with IRFs
  "lme4",            # CRE logit/Poisson for nonlinear DPD
  "fixest",          # FE Poisson and fast high-dimensional FE models
  "marginaleffects", # Average partial effects from nonlinear models
  "dplyr",           # Data manipulation
  "kableExtra"       # Formatted tables
))
```

::: {.callout-important}
## The `lag()` conflict: `plm` vs `dplyr`

`dplyr` exports `lag()` accepting only a scalar lag order. `plm` exports `lag()`
accepting a vector such as `1:2`, which `pgmm()` formulas require. Loading both
without intervention causes:

```
Error in lag(): ! n must be a whole number, not an integer vector.
```

**Fix**: add `lag <- plm::lag` once after loading both packages. The hidden
setup chunk does this for the whole document.

**Separate issue**: `plm::lag()` applied to a plain numeric vector inside
`dplyr::mutate()` returns the input **unchanged** — it does not compute a
positional lag. Always write `dplyr::lag()` explicitly inside pipelines:

```r
# Correct — positional lag within groups
df |> group_by(id) |> mutate(y_lag = dplyr::lag(y, 1))

# Wrong when lag <- plm::lag — returns y unchanged
df |> group_by(id) |> mutate(y_lag = lag(y, 1))
```
:::

### Stata commands

```stata
* ---- built-in ----
* xtset id year      declare panel structure (always first)
* xtabond           Arellano-Bond difference GMM
* xtdpdsys          System GMM (Arellano-Bover / Blundell-Bond)
* xtdpd             General DPD — most flexible built-in
* xtprobit, re      Random-effects probit
* xtpoisson         Random-effects or FE Poisson

* ---- community (ssc install) ----
ssc install xtabond2   // Roodman: collapse, orthogonal devs, diff-in-Hansen
ssc install xtlsdvc    // Bruno (2005): bias-corrected LSDV
ssc install xtpmg      // Pesaran-Shin-Smith: MG and PMG
ssc install xtdcce2    // Ditzen: dynamic CCE
ssc install xtcd2      // Ditzen: Pesaran CD test
ssc install xtslope    // Eberhardt: Pesaran-Yamagata slope homogeneity
ssc install pvar       // Abrigo-Love: panel VAR
```

## Data preparation

```{r data-r}
library(plm)
library(dplyr)
data(EmplUK)

EmplUK <- EmplUK |>
  mutate(n = log(emp), w = log(wage), k = log(capital), ys = log(output))

pdat <- pdata.frame(EmplUK, index = c("firm", "year"))

# Needed for pgmm() formulas; also set in hidden setup chunk
lag <- plm::lag

# Precomputed lag columns for plm(model = "random") formulas
pdat$n_lag1 <- plm::lag(pdat$n, 1)
pdat$n_lag2 <- plm::lag(pdat$n, 2)
pdat$w_lag1 <- plm::lag(pdat$w, 1)

pdim(pdat)
```

```stata
use abdata, clear
xtset id year
xtdescribe
xtsum n w k ys
```

## Within and between variation

```{r variance-decomp}
result <- sapply(c("n", "w", "k", "ys"),
                 function(v) panel_summary(EmplUK[[v]], EmplUK$firm))
kbl(t(result), caption = "Variance decomposition: 140 UK firms, 1976–1984") |>
  kable_styling(font_size = 13)
```

```stata
xtsum n w k ys
```

## Static panel baseline

Always bracket GMM with OLS (upward bias) and FE (downward Nickell bias).

```{r static-r}
# Precomputed lag columns avoid the swar_Between_check() failure that occurs
# when lag <- plm::lag is active and lag() is used inside an RE formula.
ols <- plm(n ~ n_lag1 + n_lag2 + w + w_lag1 + k + ys,
           data = pdat, model = "pooling")

fe  <- plm(n ~ n_lag1 + n_lag2 + w + w_lag1 + k + ys,
           data = pdat, model = "within",  effect = "twoways")

# RE with effect = "individual" — two-way RE with a lagged DV is fragile
re  <- plm(n ~ n_lag1 + n_lag2 + w + w_lag1 + k + ys,
           data = pdat, model = "random",  effect = "individual")

phtest(fe, re)
summary(fe)
```

```stata
reg  n L(1/2).n w L.w k ys i.year          // pooled OLS
xtreg n L(1/2).n w L.w k ys i.year, fe     // fixed effects
xtreg n L(1/2).n w L.w k ys,        re     // random effects (individual)
hausman fe_est re_est
```

## Anderson-Hsiao: IV estimator

```{r ah-r}
# First-difference by hand.
# dplyr::lag() must be explicit — plm::lag() on a plain vector in mutate()
# returns the input unchanged, not a positional lag.
pdat_fd <- EmplUK |>
  group_by(firm) |> arrange(year) |>
  mutate(
    Dn   = n  - dplyr::lag(n, 1),
    DLn  = dplyr::lag(n, 1) - dplyr::lag(n, 2),
    Dw   = w  - dplyr::lag(w, 1),
    ln2  = dplyr::lag(n, 2),
    DLn2 = dplyr::lag(n, 2) - dplyr::lag(n, 3)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(!is.na(DLn2))

pfd <- pdata.frame(pdat_fd, index = c("firm", "year"))

# AH: plm() accepts IV formula y ~ endog | instrument
ah_level <- plm(Dn ~ DLn + Dw | ln2  + Dw, data = pfd, model = "pooling")
ah_diff  <- plm(Dn ~ DLn + Dw | DLn2 + Dw, data = pfd, model = "pooling")
summary(ah_level)
```

```stata
ivregress 2sls D.n (D.L.n = L2.n)  D.w, vce(robust)   // level instrument
ivregress 2sls D.n (D.L.n = LD.n)  D.w, vce(robust)   // diff instrument
ivreg2    D.n (D.L.n = L2.n)       D.w, robust first   // + first-stage stats
```

## Arellano-Bond: one-step difference GMM

```{r ab1-r}
# lag() resolves to plm::lag (set in setup) — pgmm formulas work correctly
ab_one <- pgmm(
  log(emp) ~ lag(log(emp), 1:2) +
             lag(log(wage), 0:1) +
             lag(log(capital), 0:2) +
             lag(log(output), 0:2) |
             lag(log(emp), 2:99),
  data = EmplUK, effect = "twoways", model = "onestep"
)
summary(ab_one)
```

```stata
xtabond n L(0/1).w L(0/2).(k ys) yr1980-yr1984, lags(2) vce(robust)
estat abond
```

---

## Arellano-Bond: two-step with Windmeijer correction

```{r ab2-r}
ab_two <- pgmm(
  log(emp) ~ lag(log(emp), 1:2) +
             lag(log(wage), 0:1) +
             log(capital) +
             lag(log(output), 0:1) |
             lag(log(emp), 2:99),
  data = EmplUK, effect = "twoways", model = "twosteps"
)

# robust = TRUE applies Windmeijer (2005) correction — always use for two-step
summary(ab_two, robust = TRUE)
```

```stata
xtabond2 n L(1/2).n L(0/1).w k L(0/1).ys yr1980-yr1984, ///
    gmm(L.n, lag(2 99)) iv(L(0/1).w k L(0/1).ys yr1980-yr1984) ///
    twostep robust small
```

---

## Instrument management: lag depth

```{r instr-r}
# Limit to lags 2–4 to reduce instrument count
ab_lim <- pgmm(
  log(emp) ~ lag(log(emp), 1:2) + lag(log(wage), 0:1) +
             log(capital) + lag(log(output), 0:1) |
             lag(log(emp), 2:4),
  data = EmplUK, effect = "twoways", model = "twosteps"
)
summary(ab_lim, robust = TRUE)
```

**R limitation**: `plm::pgmm()` does not support instrument collapsing.
Use `xtabond2, collapse` in Stata for `O(T)` rather than `O(T²)` instruments.

```stata
xtabond2 n L(1/2).n L(0/1).w k L(0/1).ys yr1980-yr1984, ///
    gmm(L.n, lag(2 99) collapse) iv(L(0/1).w k L(0/1).ys yr1980-yr1984) ///
    twostep robust small
```

---

## System GMM: Blundell-Bond

```{r bb-r}
bb <- pgmm(
  log(emp) ~ lag(log(emp), 1) +
             lag(log(wage), 0:1) +
             lag(log(capital), 0:1) |
             lag(log(emp),     2:99) +
             lag(log(wage),    2:99) +
             lag(log(capital), 2:99),
  data = EmplUK, effect = "twoways", model = "onestep",
  transformation = "ld"   # levels + differences
)
summary(bb, robust = TRUE)
```

```stata
xtdpdsys n L(0/1).w L(0/1).k yr1980-yr1984, lags(1) twostep vce(robust)

xtabond2 n L.n L(0/1).w L(0/1).k yr1980-yr1984,          ///
    gmm(L.n, lag(2 99) collapse)                           ///
    gmm(L(0/1).w L(0/1).k, lag(2 99) collapse)            ///
    iv(yr1980-yr1984) twostep robust small
```

## Post-estimation: AR tests

```{r ar-tests-r}
mtest(ab_two, order = 1)   # should reject — mechanical from differencing
mtest(ab_two, order = 2)   # should NOT reject — key identification check
```

```stata
estat abond           // after xtabond / xtdpdsys / xtdpd
estat abond, lags(3)  // test AR(3) if needed
```

## Post-estimation: Sargan / Hansen test

```{r sargan-r}
s1 <- summary(ab_one)              # Sargan (one-step, non-robust)
s2 <- summary(ab_two, robust=TRUE) # Hansen J (two-step, Windmeijer)

cat("One-step Sargan:  stat =", round(s1$sargan$statistic, 2),
    " df =", s1$sargan$parameter,
    " p =",  round(s1$sargan$p.value, 3), "\n")
cat("Two-step Hansen:  stat =", round(s2$sargan$statistic, 2),
    " df =", s2$sargan$parameter,
    " p =",  round(s2$sargan$p.value, 3), "\n")
```

```stata
estat sargan   // xtabond2 prints Hansen automatically
```

## Post-estimation: difference-in-Hansen

```{r dih-r}
# Not available in plm::pgmm() — use xtabond2 in Stata
message("Difference-in-Hansen: available only via xtabond2 in Stata.")
```

```stata
* Specify separate gmm() blocks; xtabond2 tests each subset
xtabond2 n L.n L(0/1).w L(0/1).k yr1980-yr1984,    ///
    gmm(L.n, lag(2 99) collapse)                    ///
    gmm(L(0/1).w L(0/1).k, lag(2 99) collapse)     ///
    iv(yr1980-yr1984) twostep robust small
```

## Bias-corrected LSDV

```{r lsdvc-r}
# LSDVC (Bruno 2005) has no CRAN implementation.
# Best R approach: report FE and AB to bracket the bias-corrected estimate.
fe_lsdvc <- plm(n ~ n_lag1 + n_lag2 + w + w_lag1 + k + ys,
                data = pdat, model = "within", effect = "twoways")

ab_lsdvc <- pgmm(
  log(emp) ~ lag(log(emp), 1:2) + lag(log(wage), 0:1) +
             log(capital) | lag(log(emp), 2:4),
  data = EmplUK, effect = "twoways", model = "twosteps"
)

cat("FE  gamma1:", round(coef(fe_lsdvc)["n_lag1"], 4), "(downward-biased)\n")
cat("AB  gamma1:", round(coef(ab_lsdvc)[1],        4), "(consistent)\n")
cat("LSDVC lies between these — use xtlsdvc in Stata for the point estimate\n")
```

```stata
xtlsdvc n L.n L(0/1).w L(0/1).k yr1980-yr1984, initial(ab) vcov(500) lags(1)
xtlsdvc n L.n L(0/1).w L(0/1).k yr1980-yr1984, initial(bb) vcov(500) lags(1)
```

## Unbalanced panels and orthogonal deviations

```{r orthog-r}
library(panelvar)

# Load a private copy of EmplUK so this chunk is self-contained and does
# not overwrite the global EmplUK that downstream chunks depend on.
# data("EmplUK", envir = e) scopes the load to environment e only.
e <- new.env()
data("EmplUK", package = "plm", envir = e)
e$EmplUK$n <- log(e$EmplUK$emp)

pvgmm_fod <- pvargmm(
  dependent_vars           = c("n"),
  lags                     = 1,
  transformation           = "fod",
  data                     = e$EmplUK,
  panel_identifier         = c("firm", "year"),
  steps                    = "twostep",
  system_instruments       = FALSE,
  max_instr_dependent_vars = 4,
  min_instr_dependent_vars = 2
)
summary(pvgmm_fod)
```

```stata
xtabond2 n L.n L(0/1).w L(0/1).k yr1980-yr1984,   ///
    gmm(L.n, lag(2 99) collapse)                   ///
    iv(L(0/1).w L(0/1).k yr1980-yr1984)            ///
    twostep robust small orthogonal
```

## Panel VAR

```{r pvar-r}
library(panelvar)

# Private copy — does not touch global EmplUK
e2 <- new.env()
data("EmplUK", package = "plm", envir = e2)
e2$EmplUK$n <- log(e2$EmplUK$emp)
e2$EmplUK$w <- log(e2$EmplUK$wage)

pvar_mod <- pvargmm(
  dependent_vars           = c("n", "w"),
  lags                     = 1,
  transformation           = "fod",
  data                     = e2$EmplUK,
  panel_identifier         = c("firm", "year"),
  steps                    = "twostep",
  system_instruments       = FALSE,
  max_instr_dependent_vars = 4,
  min_instr_dependent_vars = 2
)
summary(pvar_mod)
stability(pvar_mod)

pvar_irf <- girf(pvar_mod, n.ahead = 8, ma_approx_steps = 8)
plot(pvar_irf)
```

```stata
pvar n w, lags(1) fod twostep
pvarstable
pvarirf, oirf mc(500) step(8)
pvargranger
```

## Cross-sectional dependence

```{r cd-test-r}
fe_cd <- plm(n ~ n_lag1 + n_lag2 + w + w_lag1 + k + ys,
             data = pdat, model = "within", effect = "twoways")
pcdtest(fe_cd, test = "cd")   # Pesaran (2015) CD test
pcdtest(fe_cd, test = "lm")   # LM version — better for small T
```

```stata
xtreg n L(1/2).n w L.w k ys i.year, fe
xtcd2   // ssc install xtcd2
```

## Slope heterogeneity test

```{r slope-test-r}
# The formal Pesaran-Yamagata (2008) Delta-tilde test is not on CRAN.
# This approximation runs unit-by-unit OLS and shows coefficient dispersion.
unit_coefs <- lapply(split(EmplUK, EmplUK$firm), function(d) {
  d <- d |> arrange(year) |>
    mutate(n_l1 = dplyr::lag(n, 1),
           n_l2 = dplyr::lag(n, 2),
           w_l1 = dplyr::lag(w, 1)) |>
    filter(!is.na(n_l2))
  if (nrow(d) < 5) return(NULL)
  tryCatch(coef(lm(n ~ n_l1 + n_l2 + w + w_l1 + k + ys, data = d)),
           error = function(e) NULL)
})
unit_coefs <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), unit_coefs))
cat("Coefficient of variation across units:\n")
round(apply(unit_coefs, 2, function(x) sd(x, na.rm=TRUE) / abs(mean(x, na.rm=TRUE))), 3)
```

**R limitation**: Use `xtslope` in Stata for the formal test with correct inference.

```stata
xtslope n L.n w L.w k ys   // ssc install xtslope
```

## Mean Group and CCE Mean Group

`plm::pmg()` supports `"mg"` (Mean Group), `"cmg"` (CCE-MG), and `"dmg"`
(Demeaned MG). The Pooled Mean Group estimator (Pesaran-Shin-Smith 1999) is
Stata-only via `xtpmg`.

```{r mg-cmg-r}
mg_mod  <- pmg(n ~ w + k + ys, data = pdat, model = "mg")
cmg_mod <- pmg(n ~ w + k + ys, data = pdat, model = "cmg")

summary(mg_mod)
summary(cmg_mod)

# Hausman: H0 = common factors not needed (CMG = MG asymptotically)
phtest(mg_mod, cmg_mod)
```

```stata
xtpmg d.n d.w d.k d.ys, lr(L.n w k ys) ec(ec) full mg
estimates store mg
xtpmg d.n d.w d.k d.ys, lr(L.n w k ys) ec(ec) full pmg
estimates store pmg
hausman mg pmg, sigmamore
```

## Dynamic CCE (manual approximation)

`xtdcce2` is Stata-only. This approximates CCE-MG by augmenting each unit
regression with cross-sectional means, but does not produce correct standard
errors.

```{r dcce-r}
EmplUK_aug <- EmplUK |>
  group_by(year) |>
  mutate(n_bar  = mean(n,  na.rm = TRUE),
         w_bar  = mean(w,  na.rm = TRUE),
         k_bar  = mean(k,  na.rm = TRUE),
         ys_bar = mean(ys, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ungroup()

ccemg <- lapply(split(EmplUK_aug, EmplUK_aug$firm), function(d) {
  d <- d |> arrange(year) |>
    mutate(n_l1 = dplyr::lag(n, 1),
           n_l2 = dplyr::lag(n, 2),
           w_l1 = dplyr::lag(w, 1)) |>
    filter(!is.na(n_l2))
  if (nrow(d) < 5) return(NULL)
  tryCatch(coef(lm(n ~ n_l1 + n_l2 + w + w_l1 + k + ys +
                     n_bar + w_bar + k_bar + ys_bar, data = d)),
           error = function(e) NULL)
})
ccemg <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), ccemg))
cat("CCE-MG point estimates (SEs not valid — use xtdcce2 in Stata):\n")
round(colMeans(ccemg, na.rm = TRUE), 4)
```

```stata
xtdcce2 n L.n w k ys, cr(n w k ys) cr_lags(1) mg   // ssc install xtdcce2
```

## Nonlinear DPD: data setup

```{r nonlin-setup-r}
# dplyr::lag() must be explicit — plm::lag() gives wrong values in mutate()
panel_df <- EmplUK |>
  mutate(n_hi = as.integer(n > median(n, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  group_by(firm) |> arrange(year) |>
  mutate(n_hi_lag = dplyr::lag(n_hi, 1),
         y_init   = first(n_hi),
         w_bar    = mean(w,  na.rm = TRUE),
         k_bar    = mean(k,  na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(!is.na(n_hi_lag))

cat("Observations:", nrow(panel_df), "\n")
```

```stata
xtile n_hi = n, nq(2)
replace n_hi = (n_hi == 2)
bysort id (year): gen y_init = n_hi[1]
bysort id: egen w_bar = mean(w)
bysort id: egen k_bar = mean(k)
```

## CRE dynamic logit: Wooldridge (2005)

Probit does not converge on this dataset; logit is equivalent for this approach.

```{r dynlogit-r}
library(lme4)

mod_logit <- glmer(
  n_hi ~ n_hi_lag + w + k + y_init + w_bar + k_bar + (1 | firm),
  data    = panel_df,
  family  = binomial(link = "logit"),
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
)
summary(mod_logit)

# Always report average partial effects, not latent-index coefficients.
# Requires marginaleffects package:
# avg_slopes(mod_logit, variables = c("n_hi_lag","w","k"), re.form = NA)
```

```stata
xtlogit n_hi L.n_hi w k y_init w_bar k_bar, re
margins, dydx(L.n_hi w k) predict(pr)
test y_init
```

## CRE dynamic Poisson

```{r dynpois-r}
pois_df <- EmplUK |>
  group_by(firm) |> arrange(year) |>
  mutate(emp_lag = dplyr::lag(emp, 1),
         y_init  = first(emp),
         w_bar   = mean(w, na.rm = TRUE),
         k_bar   = mean(k, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(!is.na(emp_lag))

mod_pois <- glmer(
  emp ~ emp_lag + w + k + y_init + w_bar + k_bar + (1 | firm),
  data    = pois_df,
  family  = poisson,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)
summary(mod_pois)
```

```stata
xtpoisson emp L.emp w k y_init w_bar k_bar, re
margins, dydx(*) predict(nu0)
xtpoisson emp L.emp w k, fe   // FE Poisson — no initial conditions needed
```

## Capability matrix

| Estimator / Feature | R | Stata built-in | Stata (`ssc`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anderson-Hsiao IV | `plm()` IV formula | `ivregress` | `ivreg2` |
| AB difference GMM | ✅ `pgmm` | `xtabond` | `xtabond2` |
| AB two-step + Windmeijer | ✅ `pgmm` | `xtabond` | `xtabond2` |
| System GMM (BB) | ✅ `pgmm(ld)` | `xtdpdsys` | `xtabond2` |
| Collapse instruments | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ `xtabond2` |
| Orthogonal deviations | ✅ `panelvar` | ❌ | ✅ `xtabond2` |
| Difference-in-Hansen | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ `xtabond2` |
| Sargan / Hansen $J$ | ✅ `summary(pgmm)` | `estat sargan` | ✅ `xtabond2` |
| AB AR tests | ✅ `mtest()` | `estat abond` | ✅ `xtabond2` |
| LSDVC (Bruno 2005) | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ `xtlsdvc` |
| Panel VAR + IRFs | ✅ `panelvar` | ❌ | ✅ `pvar` |
| Pesaran CD test | ✅ `pcdtest()` | ❌ | ✅ `xtcd2` |
| Slope homogeneity $\tilde\Delta$ | Manual only | ❌ | ✅ `xtslope` |
| Mean Group (MG) | ✅ `pmg("mg")` | ❌ | ✅ `xtpmg` |
| CCE Mean Group | ✅ `pmg("cmg")` | ❌ | ✅ `xtdcce2` |
| Pooled Mean Group (PMG) | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ `xtpmg` |
| Dynamic CCE | Manual (no SEs) | ❌ | ✅ `xtdcce2` |
| CRE dynamic logit | ✅ `lme4::glmer` | ✅ `xtlogit,re` | — |
| CRE dynamic probit | ✅ `lme4::glmer` | ✅ `xtprobit,re` | — |
| CRE Poisson | ✅ `lme4::glmer` | ✅ `xtpoisson,re` | — |
| FE Poisson | ✅ `fixest::fepois` | ✅ `xtpoisson,fe` | — |
| Avg. partial effects | ✅ `marginaleffects` | ✅ `margins` | — |

**Key notes**

`xtabond2` is the recommended Stata command for all GMM DPD work — it
supersedes `xtabond`, `xtdpdsys`, and `xtdpd` and is the only command with
collapsed instruments, orthogonal deviations, and difference-in-Hansen.

`plm::pgmm()` is the R workhorse but lacks collapsed instruments, orthogonal
deviations, and difference-in-Hansen. For these, use `xtabond2` in Stata.

LSDVC and Pooled Mean Group are Stata-only. Dynamic CCE has no production-quality
R implementation with correct standard errors.

Nonlinear DPD (CRE logit/Poisson) is well-handled in both environments via
`lme4::glmer()` in R and `xtlogit/xtpoisson, re` in Stata. Always report
average partial effects, not latent-index coefficients.
